knowledge_point.title: Interpreting the Derivative of a Function

question.:question/problem: Consider a sphere. Let $S$ denote the surface area and let $r$ denote the radius. The radius can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${S}^{′}(r)$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $S(r)$ gives the surface area of the sphere as a function of the radius. So,

$$
{S}^{′}(r)=\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}r}=\frac{\text{Instantaneous change in }S}{\text{Change in }r}.
$$

Therefore, ${S}^{′}(r)$ is the rate at which the surface area changes as the radius changes.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The rate at which the volume changes as the radius changes
The surface area of the sphere
The rate at which the radius changes as the surface area changes
The rate at which the surface area changes as the radius changes
The radius of the sphere
